equity_bridge.item: Honda Financial Services at 9x normalised after-tax segment profit
equity_bridge.note: Segment profit FY2024-26 ~274 / 315.6 / 275.5bn, H1 FY2027 211.0bn (lifted by lease-vehicle disposals); normalised JPY 290bn x (1 - 0.27) = 212bn x 9. Segment profit is after interest expense, so this is an equity value. Roughly 0.6-0.7x estimated finance-subsidiary book equity, consistent with a ~7% ROE against a ~10% required return. Segment assets JPY 17.29tn at 2026-09-30.

equity_bridge.item: Investments accounted for using the equity method at 0.8x book
equity_bridge.note: JPY 1,204.9bn at 2026-09-30 (Q2 FY2027 6-K). Equity income is outside operating profit and so outside the flows. 20% haircut for the Chinese automobile joint ventures (JPY 90.9bn impaired in FY2026); the motorcycle affiliates (JPY 106bn book, JPY 65bn FY2026 profit share) are worth well above book, which partly offsets.

equity_bridge.item: Listed and unlisted equity securities at fair value (FVOCI)
equity_bridge.note: Q2 FY2027 6-K fair value table, 2026-09-30 (JPY 633.9bn at 2026-03-31; holdings are being sold down). Dividend income is in finance income, outside the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at 9x normalised profit share
equity_bridge.note: JPY 80bn x 9; book value JPY 254.9bn at 2026-09-30. See nci_treatment.

equity_bridge.item: Unpaid provisions for EV-related losses, after tax
equity_bridge.note: JPY 582.7bn at 2026-09-30 (Q2 FY2027 6-K note 7: supplier and alliance compensation, onerous contract) x (1 - 0.28). Already expensed, not yet paid, so it is a debt-like claim on the cash pile rather than a future margin item.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-year CAGR (1.9%) is far below revenue 3-year CAGR (8.8%): revenue was inflated by yen depreciation while equity was reduced by JPY 1.64tn of buybacks (FY2024-26) and the FY2026 loss. Neither is used as the forward growth rate; the projection is built on industrial revenue at 1-2% beyond the FY2027 currency-driven step.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2023 16,907.7bn to FY2026 21,796.6bn. No FY2021 annual revenue row in the Metrics CSV, so the 5-year revenue CAGR is not computed. EPS CAGRs are undefined because FY2026 EPS is negative (-106.06). Equity: FY2021 9,082.3bn, FY2023 11,184.3bn, FY2026 11,817.5bn. FCF CAGRs are not computed: consolidated FCF (1,230 / 1,497 / 139 / -555 / 238bn, FY2022-26) is dominated by swings in finance receivables and leased vehicles, and the industrial-only cash flow statement is not in the extracted filings. No SBC adjustment applies.

scenario_narratives.base: The EV write-off is a finite restructuring. Management's own plan is to eliminate EV-related losses by FY2029 and redirect JPY 4.4tn to hybrids and ICE; the base case gives it partial credit. Motorcycles (JPY 732bn segment profit in FY2026, JPY 439bn in H1 FY2027, ~19% margin) ease to roughly JPY 780bn as the yen and Asian demand normalise, automobiles recover only to ~2% (FY2025 was 1.7%, FY2024 4.1%), giving a 5.3% industrial operating margin against 6.4% in FY2024 and 4.9% in FY2025. Revenue steps up 8.8% in FY2027 on currency and North American volume (H1 industrial revenue +11.8%), then grows 1-2%. Year 1 free cash flow is negative on the JPY 1.25tn capex plan. Management's FY2029 record-profit and FY2031 10% ROIC targets are not assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The hybrid pivot works and the tariff burden eases: the underlying 9.2% industrial margin of H1 FY2027 proves partly durable, North American hybrids (CR-V, Civic, Accord) hold share and price, automobiles reach ~4.5% and motorcycles keep ~19-20% on a growing India and ASEAN base, for a 7.0% industrial operating margin, above the FY2024 peak and in line with management's FY2031 ROIC ambition. Growth of 3-4% for several years on motorcycle volume and mix. This needs the automobile recovery, the motorcycle margin and the currency all to hold at once.
scenario_narratives.bear: The automobile business is structurally impaired rather than restructuring: further EV-related charges land in FY2028-29 beyond what is provided (the 20-F warns of additional losses in FY2027 'and later'), Chinese makers take share in ASEAN and other export markets after already collapsing Honda's China joint-venture volumes (Asia group unit sales -36% in H1 FY2027), US tariffs stay, and a stronger yen removes the translation tailwind. Automobiles sit at or below break-even, motorcycles fade toward JPY 650bn as electric two-wheelers and local competitors pressure India and Indonesia, and the industrial operating margin settles at 2.5%. Revenue shrinks in yen and then stagnates. The finance arm and cash pile still carry most of the value, which is why the bear case sits near the market price rather than far below it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Honda is valued as three things: an industrial cash-flow stream (motorcycles carrying a weak automobile business), a captive lender worth roughly 0.6-0.7x its book, and a balance sheet with about JPY 3.4tn of industrial net cash plus affiliates and securities. At the current price the market capitalisation of about JPY 7.2tn leaves under JPY 2tn for the entire industrial business after net cash and the bridge, about 2x normal motorcycle operating profit; the market is pricing the bear case. The value gap is real but it is the familiar Japanese-automaker gap: it closes only if the cash is returned or the automobile business stops destroying it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Industrial net cash is ~45% of the current market value and is estimated, not disclosed: finance-subsidiary cash (assumed JPY 400bn) and the 2026-09-30 industrial debt (assumed JPY 1.69tn) are both estimates. Each JPY 100bn error is about USD 0.48 per ADS.
The cash may not reach shareholders: JPY 925.7bn of capex in H1 FY2027 alone, JPY 6.2tn of planned resource investment over FY2027-29, and buybacks stopped in FY2027 after JPY 1.39tn in FY2025-26.
Further EV-related losses beyond the JPY 582.7bn provided; the 20-F states additional losses are expected in FY2027 and possibly later.
Motorcycle margins (~19%) are at record levels and supply more than all of industrial profit; a 5-point fall is worth roughly JPY 225bn of operating profit a year.
Currency: flows are translated at about JPY 160 per USD. A stronger yen cuts yen revenue and margin, though it raises the USD value of each yen of intrinsic value.
Financial Services is valued on earnings, not book: residual-value losses on leased EVs (impairments already taken in FY2026) and US consumer credit are the swing factors.
US tariff policy on Japan, Canada and Mexico-built vehicles.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 23.25-36.88. FX and Tokyo-line parity per inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: Form 20-F for FY2026 (HMC_Annual_FY2026.txt: segment note, EV-loss note 4(d), provisions note 17, liquidity section, capex plan); Form 6-K for the six months ended 2026-09-30 (HMC_Quarterly_Q2-FY2027.txt: balance sheet, segment note, provisions, fair value table); HMC_Metrics.csv.
data_sources.qualitative: 20-F Item 5 strategy discussion (three-year plan to FY2029, ROIC target FY2031). HMC_Analysis.json (risks, FY2027 guidance, recent developments).

inputs.sbc_source: None material. FY2026 20-F statement of changes in equity shows share-based payment transactions of JPY (405)m (BIP trust for directors); treated as zero. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null.
inputs.fx_note: USD/JPY 159.686 (Yahoo JPY=X, 2026-11-13T21:59Z), so model->quote fx_rate = 1/159.686 = 0.0062623 USD per JPY. Parity check against the Tokyo line: 7267.T JPY 1,841.5 (2026-11-13 close) x 3 shares per ADS / 159.686 = USD 34.60 against the NYSE ADS close at inputs.price_as_of, a 0.9% tie across a 15-hour gap. That one line confirms the rate, its direction and the 3:1 ADS ratio.
inputs.ads_ratio_note: 1 ADS = 3 shares of common stock (FY2026 20-F cover and Item 9: 'each American Depositary Share representing three shares of Common Stock'). The ratio moved from 1:1 to 1:3 alongside the 3-for-1 split of 2023-10-01, which is why the ADS price did not split. NOT 1:1.
inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalents: 3,892.909m common shares outstanding ex-treasury (implied by H1 FY2027 EPS, 516,761 / 132.75, and matching the Q2 FY2027 weighted count) divided by 3 = 1,297.636m ADS. No dilutive securities (20-F note 24: basic and diluted EPS identical). Held flat: no SBC, and buybacks are not assumed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% in every scenario: the house reference for JPY-reporting Japanese industrials (JPY risk-free ~1.5-2% plus a ~6% ERP at beta ~1.1, nudged up because roughly two-thirds of Honda's operating flows are earned in USD and Asian currencies and only translated into JPY). Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights; no scenario-specific WACC and no ad-hoc premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal (JPY 80.2bn FY2026) plus lease interest carried as lease_cost_pct_path 0.45% of industrial revenue; lease liabilities (JPY 326.9bn at 2026-03-31) excluded from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI is deducted once, in the equity bridge, at 9x a JPY 80bn normalised NCI profit share (FY2024-26: 75.4 / 67.2 / 70.9bn; H1 FY2027 43.4bn) rather than at its JPY 254.9bn book value, because the minorities sit in the high-return Asian motorcycle and automobile subsidiaries and take ~100% of their profit share out as dividends (JPY 78.2bn paid FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_note: INDUSTRIAL (non-financial-services) net cash only. Cash = consolidated JPY 5,503.8bn at 2026-09-30 less an ESTIMATED JPY 400bn held inside the finance subsidiaries (not disclosed in the 20-F or 6-K; the finance arm's cash is valued inside its own line in the bridge). Debt = the 20-F's disclosed 'liabilities associated with funding for non-Financial services businesses' of JPY 1,238.8bn at 2026-03-31, rolled forward by an ESTIMATED JPY ~450bn of H1 FY2027 industrial borrowing (consolidated net financing proceeds of JPY 695bn against a finance book that was flat in yen). Cross-check: the same definition at 2026-03-31 on disclosed debt gives JPY 3,428bn net cash against JPY 3,414bn here. The JPY 12.25tn of finance-subsidiary funding is NOT debt of the industrial business: it funds JPY 16.3tn of receivables and leased vehicles and is netted inside the financial-services value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum-of-parts through the owner-FCF Drivers engine. (1) Industrial operations (Motorcycle + Automobile + Power Products) valued by component owner-FCF DCF on revenue EXCLUDING the Financial Services segment, with industrial net cash. (2) Honda Financial Services valued separately in the equity bridge at capitalised after-tax segment profit (segment profit is already after funding cost, so it is an equity flow and its debt is never deducted). (3) Equity-method affiliates, listed equity holdings, NCI, pension deficit and unpaid EV provisions in the bridge. A pure consolidated owner-FCF DCF is wrong here (consolidated OCF contains receivable and lease-fleet growth; consolidated debt is 91% captive-finance funding) and a pure bank model is wrong too (80%+ of revenue is manufacturing). FY2026 LOSS: operating loss JPY 414.3bn includes JPY 1,453.7bn of EV-related charges in operating profit (plus 124.1bn in equity-method), from cancelling North American EV programmes; H1 FY2027 carried a further JPY 484.9bn. These are treated as a finite restructuring, not the run-rate: underlying industrial operating margin was 6.4% FY2024, 4.9% FY2025, 4.2% FY2026 and 9.2% in H1 FY2027 (flattered by tariff effects and a JPY ~160 yen). The unpaid cash tail is charged in the bridge and the bear case carries structural automobile losses. reported_fcf / last_fcf are CONSOLIDATED figures from the Metrics CSV (OCF less PP&E and intangible additions, then less interest income) and are kept for the audit identity only; they are contaminated by the finance arm and are not the base of the projection, which is built from industrial revenue and margins. Estimated industrial owner FCF was ~JPY 700bn FY2024 and ~JPY 300bn FY2025. TIMING: the balance sheet is 2026-09-30 while year 1 is the whole of FY2027, so H1 FY2027 cash flow (negative on an industrial basis: JPY 925.7bn of capex including the Ohio facility purchase, and JPY 548bn of EV provision payments) is in both; the overlap is conservative. GUIDANCE: FY2027 company forecast as raised at Q1 (per HMC_Analysis.json; not in the extracted 6-Ks): revenue JPY 24,150bn, operating profit JPY 650bn, EV-related losses ~JPY 520bn, adjusted operating profit ~JPY 1.17tn, at ~JPY 155 per USD. H1 FY2027 alone delivered JPY 648.7bn reported and JPY 1,133.6bn ex-EV, so that guide is stale or assumes a very weak H2; year 1 is set between the two (industrial operating margin 3.7% base) with the 20-F capex plan of JPY 1,250bn. Whether the guide was changed with the Q2 release should be checked. EPS SPLIT BASIS: the CSV's FY2022 (137.03) and FY2023 (128.01) EPS are already post-split (reported 411.09 and 384.02 pre-split); quarterly EPS for FY2016-FY2021 also look post-split against net income and ~5.2-5.4bn shares.

bear.margin_note: Implied industrial operating margin 2.5 / 2.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5% then flat at 2.5%. Year 1 is still above the ~1.3% implied by company guidance.

base.margin_note: EBITDA margin = industrial operating margin + D&A ex right-of-use + lease cost. Implied industrial operating margin 3.7 / 4.8 / 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3% then flat at 5.3%. Year 1 = H1 FY2027 actual industrial operating profit of JPY 437.8bn plus an H2 at ~4% underlying less ~JPY 100bn of further EV charges; this sits well above what company guidance implies (~1.3%) because H1 alone already reached the full-year guide.
base.capex_note: Year 1: 20-F plan of JPY 1,250bn (H1 cash JPY 825bn including the Ohio facility purchase) plus ~JPY 210bn capitalised development. Thereafter capex settles slightly above D&A.
base.tax_note: 33% of industrial EBIT: above the ~30% statutory rate because losses in Japan and China automobile operations do not shelter profits taxed in Asia and North America. Consolidated cash tax was JPY 413-541bn a year in FY2024-26.

bull.margin_note: Implied industrial operating margin 4.5 / 5.8 / 6.3 / 6.7 / 7.0% then flat at 7.0%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: the automobile turnaround is an unproven pivot announced only in March 2026, the company itself flags further EV losses, and the base case already rests on record motorcycle margins and a very weak yen. Base 50%: a partial recovery to below the FY2024 margin. Bull cut to 20% from 35% because it needs three independent things (automobile margin, motorcycle margin, currency) to go right together.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
